articles.title: Ben Affleck is an AI nerd, and the internet is impressed
articles.summary: Actor Ben Affleck has gone viral after showcasing his surprisingly deep technical knowledge of artificial intelligence across several recent interview clips.
articles.paragraph: Hollywood star Ben Affleck has surprised the internet by going viral with video clips showing his comprehensive understanding of artificial intelligence technology. Earlier this year, the actor sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix for a reported, though disputed, 587 million dollars. During recent interviews, Affleck broke down complex concepts such as convolutional neural networks, transformers, and tensors, revealing that he writes basic Python code. He explained that he previously spent eight months shooting footage to build a proprietary dataset, allowing creators to ethically fine-tune open-source models for discrete cinematic tasks. Affleck even integrated these tailored AI tools into the post-production workflow for his own film, Animals. Rather than fearing science-fiction doomsday scenarios, he views artificial intelligence as an additive filmmaking tool rather than an industry replacement. Instead, he highlighted grounded concerns regarding education and youth, citing learned helplessness and a thirty percent increase in top college grades.

articles.title: OpenAI’s revenue is reportedly $20 billion less than previously projected
articles.summary: OpenAI reportedly informed investors that its annualized revenue is approaching $50 billion, roughly $20 billion lower than previously estimated.
articles.paragraph: OpenAI recently told investors that its annualized revenue is nearing $50 billion, down $20 billion from prior expectations. Just over a week ago, reports suggested the artificial intelligence laboratory was approaching a $70 billion run rate to rival competitor Anthropic. According to the Financial Times, that earlier estimate stemmed from investors trying to mirror Anthropic's metrics, which factor in third-party cloud partner sales that OpenAI excludes. Demonstrating top-line growth remains a persistent challenge as the company attempts to validate the enormous financial backing it receives. OpenAI raised a massive $122 billion during a March funding round alone. Additionally, leaked financial records for 2025 revealed the business brought in about $13 billion while spending significantly more. Amid these financial realities, the company has now delayed its previously rumored initial public offering from this year to early 2027.

articles.title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference
articles.summary: Anthropic's updated usage policy explicitly prohibits users from repeatedly abusing Claude in extreme cases, though ordinary frustration and criticism are still allowed.
articles.paragraph: Anthropic's updated usage policy explicitly prohibits users from repeatedly abusing Claude in extreme cases, though ordinary frustration and criticism are still allowed. The new rules also address election interference, deceptive campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance. Anthropic updated its usage policy on Thursday, codifying new prohibitions on election interference, weapons software, and surveillance. But perhaps the most attention-getting change is a new prohibition against prolonged verbal abuse of the model, which is now expressly forbidden. Since an update in August, Claude has been trained to end conversations with “persistently harmful or abusive user interactions” — but the new policy explicitly bars users from pursuing those conversations.

articles.title: The Atari 800XL hybrid gaming console is back after decades in obscurity
articles.summary: Atari is bringing back its classic 800XL hybrid computer and console with modern upgrades, twenty-five built-in games, and a 220-dollar price tag.
articles.paragraph: Hardware maker Plaion Replai has revived the classic Atari 800XL as a modern hybrid gaming console and personal computer. Originally a refresh of a 1979 design, the successful eight-bit computer lineup was retired in the early 1990s before receiving this new overhaul. The recreated system features contemporary upgrades, including HDMI output, several USB ports, and a period-accurate rechargeable joystick. Players receive 25 pre-installed titles like Centipede and Missile Command, along with a functional cartridge slot and the ability to load Atari 400 and 5200 software via USB. Retaining its computing roots, the machine incorporates a full-sized mechanical keyboard and supports the Atari Basic programming platform. This setup enables owners to build their own software and run vintage 1980s homebrew projects. Priced at $220, the reimagined device is currently available for preorder ahead of its planned April 23, 2027 shipping date.

articles.title: New study shows concerning rise in developer burnout — and growing distrust in how AI may affect their jobs
articles.summary: Worldwide developer survey reveals growing concerns over AI and an army of coders who feel close to burning out.
articles.paragraph: The stack is overflowing with fatigue... Stack Overflow’s annual survey is a useful look at how developers feel about the industry they work in, and highlights a growing friction between traditional software development and the growing role of AI tools. The survey, by the Stack Overflow coding question-and-answer platform, also highlights a growth in solo employment, with 10.5% of respondents stating they freelance or are sole proprietors of a business, up from 3.9% in the previous years’ survey. One key takeaway from the survey is that 45.1% of developers state they are “complacent” in their current roles, with around a third (32.6%) of respondents describing themselves as “unhappy” (just 22.3% are “happy.”) Of that 45.1% figure, burnout or fatigue were cited as the main cause (21.1%).

articles.title: Almost 300,000 people now live in flood‑prone areas in the Nepalese Himalayas—new research
articles.summary: On Aug. 26, a rock and ice avalanche triggered a huge flood that swept through a steep valley in Nepal, leaving thousands dead and missing.
articles.paragraph: On Aug. 26, a rock and ice avalanche triggered a huge flood that swept through a steep valley in Nepal, leaving thousands dead and missing. It was an extreme example of a growing problem across the Himalayas. As glaciers melt, glacial lakes expand and mountain permafrost thaws, the risks from floods, landslides and other high-mountain hazards are increasing. At the same time, more people and infrastructure are moving into the valleys where these hazards are most likely to strike.

articles.title: Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Worth $8.3 Million Moves After 16 Years
articles.summary: A batch of 100.02 BTC mined in July 2010 moved Wednesday after 16 years. It's worth about $8.3 million, but nothing in the transaction shows who owns it.
articles.paragraph: A batch of Bitcoin mined in July 2010 moved Wednesday after 16 years. It's worth about $8.3 million, but data doesn't show who owns it. A batch of 100.02 Bitcoin mined in July 2010, from a period commonly known as the Satoshi-era, moved on Wednesday for the first time in 16 years. At roughly $83,000 per coin, the stash was worth about $8.3 million when it left. Based on Bitbo’s highest registered price of BTC in 2010, the stash was worth around $29 when it was mined. The transaction was confirmed at 18:52 UTC in block 970,379—one of the batches of transactions that Bitcoin's network stamps onto its public ledger roughly every 10 minutes.

articles.title: Solana DeFi Firms Orca and Loopscale Merge Under New Formation Brand
articles.summary: Solana DEX Orca and lending platform Loopscale will operate as Formation, a New York company aiming to finance AI, energy, robotics and defense assets and eventually reach regulated U.S. markets.
articles.paragraph: Solana DEX Orca and lending platform Loopscale will operate as Formation, a New York company aiming to finance AI, energy, and robotics. Solana decentralized exchange Orca and lending protocol Loopscale are merging into a single company called Formation, the two teams announced Wednesday. The new firm is headquartered in New York and led by Loopscale co-founder Luke Truitt as CEO, with fellow co-founder Mary Gooneratne as chief operating officer and Orca's Christopher Montagano as chief strategy and legal officer. Neither announcement discloses financial terms. Formation pairs Orca's trading infrastructure with Loopscale's credit order book and vaults, so an issuer can launch an asset with trading and credit live from day one, according to Loopscale's FAQ.
